title: WorkMux plugin manifest (workmux-plugin.json), version 1
description: Everything WorkMux needs to build and run a project plugin: a Docker image with an MCP server inside that bots use as an MCP server. Put it into the root (or a subdirectory) of a git repository and add the plugin in Project settings → Plugins with the repository URL.

$schema.description: URL of this schema, so editors can validate and complete the manifest.

pluginVersion.description: Version of the plugin itself (semver, e.g. 1.4.0) — not of this format. WorkMux compares it with the installed one and offers an update when the repository has a higher one. Without it the version is the commit of the build.

changelog.description: What changed in this version — a short text or an https:// URL of the release notes. Shown next to the update offer.

slug.description: Short id of the plugin. Bots see its MCP tools as <slug>__<tool>, so it is a DNS label: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, at most 40 characters.

description.description: What the plugin does — shown to people and to bots.

instructions.description: How a bot should use the plugin: which files it takes, the typical workflow, how to get the result out.

build.description: Build the image from a Dockerfile in this repository. Exactly one of build or image.

dockerfile.description: Path of the Dockerfile, relative to the build context. Default Dockerfile.

context.description: Build context directory, relative to the directory of this manifest. It must stay inside the repository. Default ".".

args.description: Build arguments { NAME: value }. Not for secrets — they end up in the image history.

image.description: A ready image in a registry instead of build, e.g. ghcr.io/org/plugin:1.2.3 (pulled with the project's registry logins). Exactly one of build or image.

mcp.description: Where the MCP server (streamable HTTP) listens inside the container. It must listen on 0.0.0.0, not localhost.

port.description: TCP port of the MCP server inside the container.

path.description: URL path of the MCP endpoint. Default /mcp.

resources.description: Requested limits of one container. The project and the machine cap them; empty = the machine default for a sidecar.

gpu.description: NVIDIA GPU for the container: "none" = no GPU (default), "optional" = use the GPU when the machine has one, otherwise run without it, "required" = do not run on a machine without a GPU (the build and the MCP test still run there, without the GPU). The container gets WORKMUX_GPU=1 when it got the GPU, otherwise 0. An unknown value is read as "none".

idleMinutes.description: Minutes of inactivity in a conversation after which its container and its /work volume are deleted. Default 30.

env.description: Plain environment variables { NAME: value } of the container. No secrets — declare those in secrets. PATH, HOME, HOSTNAME and WORKMUX_* are reserved.

secrets.description: Secret environment variables the plugin needs. Only names here — the values are picked from the project's passwords in the plugin settings.

description.description: What the secret is (shown next to the password picker).

required.description: The plugin cannot run without it — the build fails until a value is set. Default true.

optional.description: The plugin runs without it (e.g. an alternative to an OAuth credential) — the build and the MCP test pass without a value. Same as required: false; do not combine with required: true.

oauth.description: OAuth credentials of the project the plugin uses. WorkMux adds a fresh access token of the credential shared with the bot to every MCP request as the given header — never into the environment of the container. The token expires; read it from each request, do not cache it.

provider.description: Slug of the provider: a preset (google, github, microsoft, slack, slack-user, notion) or a custom service the project connects through discovery / DCR.

header.description: Lowercase name of the request header that carries the access token, e.g. x-workmux-oauth-token.

scopes.description: Scopes the plugin needs. A preset takes short names from its catalog (drive, spreadsheets, repo …) or full scopes; WorkMux asks for them when connecting and reports the missing ones.

optional.description: The plugin works without this credential too — the header is then just left out. Default false.

issuer.description: Only for a custom service: HTTPS URL of the authorization server, so WorkMux can discover it and register a client (DCR) when connecting.

description.description: What the plugin does with the account (shown next to the Connect button).

files.description: Files the plugin takes and returns (in /work). Informs bots.

events.description: Events of an outside service (a new Slack message, a mention …) the plugin can deliver to the bot. When the plugin is attached to a bot, WorkMux creates a webhook URL for it and calls the subscribe tool of the plugin with { url, kinds } — the plugin registers the URL at the service. Incoming events wake the bot like a webhook monitor; the plugin container does not have to run for that.

subscribe.description: MCP tools of the plugin that register and remove the webhook URL at the service.

tool.description: Tool called with { url, kinds } after the plugin is attached to a bot. It returns { registered: true, subscription? } when it registered the URL, or { registered: false, steps: ["…"] } with the steps a person has to do at the service (e.g. paste the URL into the settings of a Slack app).

unsubscribe.description: Tool called with { url, subscription } when the plugin is detached from the bot or deleted. Best effort — WorkMux stops accepting the URL either way.

verify.description: How WorkMux checks that an event really comes from the service. Requests with a wrong signature get 401 and never wake the bot.

scheme.description: Signature scheme: slack-v0 (X-Slack-Signature with X-Slack-Request-Timestamp) or github-sha256 (X-Hub-Signature-256).

secretEnv.description: Name of a secret from secrets whose value is the signing secret of the service (e.g. SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET).

kinds.description: Kinds of events the plugin subscribes to — passed to the subscribe tool and shown to people and to the bot.

type.description: Event type as the service names it, e.g. message or app_mention.

filter.description: jq expression that keeps only the events the bot should see (as in a webhook monitor), e.g. select(.event.type == "app_mention"). Empty = every request.

extract.description: jq expression that turns the payload into the line the bot reads (as in a webhook monitor). Empty = the whole payload.

dedupKey.description: jq expression with a unique id of the event, so a retry of the service does not wake the bot twice, e.g. .event_id. Empty = a hash of the body.

persist.description: Directories whose data outlive the conversation, the container and updates of the plugin (unlike /work). Each is a Docker volume on the machine of the plugin, shared by the whole project or kept per bot; it is deleted only with the plugin (or the bot).

path.description: Absolute directory in the container, e.g. /data. Not /work and not inside it.

scope.description: "project" = one volume for the whole project, "bot" = one volume per bot (a session gets its own).

migrate.description: Command of the new version run once over the persist volumes during an update, after its MCP test and before the switch. A non-zero exit keeps the previous version. It must be idempotent and keep the data readable by the previous version — a rollback does not undo it.

command.description: Command and its arguments (exec form), e.g. ["node", "migrate.js"]. Gets WORKMUX_MIGRATE_FROM and WORKMUX_MIGRATE_TO.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long the command may run. Default 300.

type.description: File extension without the dot (stl) or a MIME type (model/stl).
